parsedVerdict.reasoning: The layer model places this file in the application layer because it matches both **/dto/** and *.dto.ts. Its one class, GetUserNotificationsDto, only describes a query and checks its input: page and limit for pagination, plus an optional status filter. That matches the role of an application DTO. It does not read or write data, handle routes or requests itself, or contain domain logic. The decorators come from class-validator, class-transformer and @nestjs/swagger. They only declare type conversion, input limits and API documentation; they do not run any framework behaviour. The page and limit bounds (at least 1, at most 100) are checks on the request, not business rules. The Swagger decorators are documentation for the API's interface, which brings in a little presentation metadata. NestJS projects normally put this on DTOs, and the project's layer model deliberately puts DTOs in the application layer. So this is not a responsibility that belongs to a different layer kind.
